mechanism: The parent assigns one constant prev_video per user in validation (the last train-positive video), which is always present in the train-built vocab and therefore gives every valid row a clean, in-distribution V[prev]·V[video] interaction — a learned per-video ranking bias. The candidate makes prev_video vary row-by-row using valid positives, but two things go wrong: (1) valid-only video_ids that were never a positive in train are absent from the train-built prev_video vocab and silently map to UNK, replacing the learned interaction with a constant UNK interaction for a large fraction of rows; (2) even for in-vocab values, the FM learned its V[prev]·V[video] interaction exclusively on train→train transitions, so valid→valid transitions are out-of-distribution and the dot-product is miscalibrated. The net effect is that the prev_video field shifts from a consistent learned ranking signal to a noisy mix of UNK and OOD interactions, degrading within-user ordering. The 7.3-σ drop is too large to be seed noise; it is a systematic feature-distribution break.
transferable_lesson: In this FM with a train-only vocab, any causal-history feature value that references an entity (video_id, author_id) not seen as a positive in train will silently become UNK and kill the interaction signal; before making a history feature row-varying at inference, verify that the entity pool at inference is a subset of the training vocab, or expand the vocab to cover it.
next_experiment: Rebuild the prev_video vocab from the union of train AND valid positive video_ids (i.e., add valid positives to the vocab before encoding), keep the candidate's chronological valid construction, and re-run the 3-seed ensemble. If primary recovers to ≥ 0.603 the loss was purely a vocab-coverage artifact and the chronological signal is real; if it stays below 0.603 the valid→valid transition distribution shift is the true problem and the parent's constant-per-user prev_video is the correct construction for this architecture, in which case the next step is to add a second history field (e.g., prev_author) built the same constant-per-user way to get additional in-vocab interaction signal without introducing OOD values.

mechanism: On the valid split the K=20 history is a pure function of (user, time) and every train positive precedes every valid impression, so bisect_right returns the full train list for all of a user's valid rows — the 20 history fields are therefore IDENTICAL across a user's items. That leaves only the 20×4 hist×{video,author,tab,dur} interactions as a within-user-reordering channel, and those pair a mostly-UNK, sparsely-trained history embedding (most users have <20 train positives, so most slots are UNK) with the base item embedding — i.e. noise, not signal. The 20 added embedding tables (each ~vocab_size×k params) also buy overfitting capacity: valid primary peaks at epoch 1 (0.592) and falls monotonically to 0.549 by epoch 5, so even the best epoch is below the parent's 0.6015. Net: user-constant, UNK-diluted recency fields add variance and overfitting rather than within-user ranking signal.
transferable_lesson: In this FM, any history that is a function of (user, time) only is constant within a user on valid and can reorder items only via hist×item interactions, which are mostly UNK and undertrained at K=20 — so to get real history signal you must make it candidate-conditioned (target-aware), not add more user-constant recency slots.
next_experiment: Replace the K=20 separate-field history with DIN-style target-aware attention: for each candidate, compute softmax(sim(candidate_video_emb, history_video_emb)) over the user's K=20 positive-history embeddings and use the weighted sum as one context vector (added to the FM input / as one extra field), keeping the same causal train-only(train+valid for test) construction. Confirm if valid primary recovers above the parent's 0.6015 (proves the constancy/UNK mechanism was the culprit); refute if it stays <=0.5936, which would mean the history signal itself is the bottleneck and we should pivot to IPS debiasing with log_random_valid.csv or multi-task.

mechanism: The edit changed nothing the model actually learns — identical 5 fields, identical FM architecture, identical loss, k, lr, and early-stopping — so the within-user ordering behaviour is the same as the parent. The only thing that changed is that the reported valid score is now the mean of three independent training runs (seeds 42/123/2024) instead of one (seed 0). Averaging independent draws of the same model family lowers the variance of the score estimate, so the number is less likely to be a lucky or unlucky single draw. For this to be a genuine gain, seed 0 would have had to be a below-average draw and the 3-seed mean would have had to sit above it — plausible, but the per-seed best values (0.6019 / 0.6017 / 0.6021) all cluster within ~0.001 of the parent's 0.6015, which is exactly what you expect if all four are samples of one distribution. No new ranking signal was introduced, so no mechanism for a real metric improvement is supported by this data; the +0.0011 (1.4 std) is consistent with variance reduction of the estimate rather than an improvement in the model.
transferable_lesson: Treat 3-seed prediction-averaging as a variance-reduction floor to apply to every candidate, not as a source of signal — read its valid-metric delta as noise, and keep the ensembled candidate as the best checkpoint because it has the same expected test performance at lower test variance (every single-seed candidate in this campaign collapsed on test).
next_experiment: On top of this now-robust 3-seed baseline, add ONE mean-pooled history vector as a new FM field: for each impression, mean-pool the embeddings of the user's last K=20 long_view-positive videos (causal, train-only for valid / train+valid for test) and train the same 3-seed ensemble. This isolates the pooling hypothesis — the campaign already showed separate recency fields are redundant (last-3-videos 0.6026, no compounding), so a single pooled vector is the clean test of whether history-as-a-vector adds signal. Confirm if valid primary > 0.6046 (i.e. > 0.6026 + 0.002) over the 3 seeds; refute if within 0.002, which would mean pooled history is also redundant and the next move should be target-aware (family-b) retrieval rather than more recency fields.

mechanism: The shared video_id embedding table makes the FM second-order interaction V[candidate_video]·V[history_video_i] target-dependent: for a fixed user, different candidate videos produce different dot products with the same 5 history embeddings, so the score is no longer user-constant and CAN reorder items within a user. This is the correct mechanism for target-aware history in an FM. However, the effect is too weak to clear the noise floor because (a) K=5 limits the information content, (b) the interaction is a single unweighted dot product per history slot with no learned gating, (c) users with fewer than 5 train positives get UNK slots that contribute a constant (the UNK embedding) that cannot differentiate candidates, and (d) the dominant user_id×video_id cross already captures most of the within-user ranking signal, leaving little headroom for a 5-slot dot-product to add. For the +0.0017 to be a real effect, the target-aware interaction would need to be strong enough to shift the relative ordering of the top-5 items for a meaningful fraction of users; at 2.1σ it is indistinguishable from the seed-to-seed variance of the ensemble itself.
transferable_lesson: In this FM, sharing the target's embedding table is the necessary and correct way to make history fields target-aware (breaking user-constancy), but a plain K=5 dot-product interaction is below the signal-to-noise floor; any further history work must either scale K up substantially (≥20) or add a learned non-linear readout on the K interaction scores before expecting a detectable gain.
next_experiment: Keep the shared-embedding mechanism but (1) sweep K ∈ {10, 20, 50} to test whether the signal is simply too sparse at K=5, and (2) replace the implicit FM dot-product with an explicit learned weighting: compute the K dot products d_i = V[candidate]·V[hist_i], pass them through a 2-layer MLP (K→16→1) with a sigmoid output, and add the result as a scalar feature to the FM logit. If K=20 or K=50 with the plain dot product still stays within ±0.0016 of parent, the bottleneck is the unweighted interaction and the MLP variant should show a clear separation; if K=50 plain dot product jumps >0.002, the bottleneck was simply K and no non-linearity is needed.

mechanism: Doubling K from 5 to 10 adds five more history slots. For users with ≥10 long_view positives in train, these carry real video IDs and add genuine target-aware FM interaction terms (V[target]·V[hist_i]). For users with 5–9 positives, the new slots are partially real and partially UNK. Crucially, even the UNK slots are NOT ranking-neutral in an FM: adding a field with embedding e_unk changes the interaction term by S_old·e_unk, which is target-dependent (S_old includes the target video's embedding), so UNK slots weakly re-rank within-user via a shared linear probe. However, this signal is extremely weak (one shared vector, same for all users) and is swamped by the dominant user_id×video_id cross that already captures most learnable signal. The net effect of five extra slots—some real, some UNK, all interacting through the same shared video_id embedding space—is a perturbation far smaller than the 0.0008 seed-to-seed variance. No mechanism for a systematic gain is supported: the +0.0002 delta is 0.25σ, indistinguishable from the stochastic trajectory of Adam updates over 13–16 epochs.
transferable_lesson: In this FM architecture, history slots share the video_id embedding space, so adding more slots does not add new representational capacity—it only adds more instances of the same pairwise dot-product pattern; the binding constraint is the embedding dimension (k=16) and the single shared video_id space, not the number of history positions, so sweeping K further (15, 25, 50) will not unlock new signal and will only increase UNK dilution and training noise.
next_experiment: Replace the K separate history slots with a single mean-pooled history embedding that is learned in its OWN embedding space (a new field with its own row in V, not reusing video_id's row). Concretely: compute the mean of the last-K video_id embeddings (in the existing space) as a continuous vector, then add it as a new dense feature that the FM treats as one additional field with a dedicated embedding row. This decouples the history signal from the target-aware pairwise interaction (which is already captured by the user_id×video_id cross) and instead lets the FM learn a history→outcome mapping independent of the target. If valid primary moves by >0.002, it confirms the history signal was being diluted by sharing the video_id embedding space; if it does not move, the history signal itself is the bottleneck and the next step is target-aware retrieval (DIN-style attention) rather than more pooling variants.

mechanism: No mechanism is supported by this data (−0.0010, 1.3σ). The hypothesis was that the shared video_id embedding space forced a compromise between the target-role and history-role representations of the same video, and that giving history its own block would let each role learn a better vector. For this to have produced a detectable gain, the two roles' optimal embeddings would have had to be far enough apart in the k=16 space that the compromise was measurably suboptimal. The flat result indicates the shared space was not a binding constraint. A structural reason the decoupling was a no-op: the FM's interaction term is a symmetric dot product (V[a]·V[b] = V[b]·V[a]) and its first-order terms are additive (W[a]+W[b]). Within a user the K history rows are constants that shift the baseline; they affect relative video ordering only through their dot product with the target row. Swapping which rows the history uses (shared vs. separate block) does not break the symmetry of that computation — the model still computes one scalar per target–history pair, and the extra |vocab|×k parameters did not translate into better within-user ranking. The binding constraint is the symmetric interaction structure, not the parameter sharing.
transferable_lesson: In this FM, structural decoupling of embedding rows (shared vs. separate block for history) is a no-op for within-user ranking because the FM's dot product treats both roles identically; to extract more from history the interaction itself must be made asymmetric (e.g., a learned k×k mixing matrix so the history contribution becomes V[target]·W_hist·V[hist]) or injected through a different architectural path (cosine-similarity features, a small MLP head over [V[target], V[hist], V[target]⊙V[hist]]).
next_experiment: Revert to the shared-space structure (parent) and sweep K_HIST ∈ {1, 5, 20, 50} with all other hyperparameters fixed, reporting valid primary for each K. Rationale: this isolates history depth as the single variable and directly tests whether the signal is saturated at K=1–2 or still growing. If all four K values land within 0.002 of each other, depth is not a lever and the next step is to make the target–history interaction asymmetric (add a learned k×k matrix W_hist so the history term becomes V[target]·W_hist·V[hist] instead of the symmetric V[target]·V[hist]; confirm by checking that the asymmetric version beats the symmetric one by >0.002 on valid). If K=50 > K=10 > K=1 by >0.002 each, depth matters and the next step is K=100 or attention-weighted pooling over the full history. If K=1 > K=10, the extra slots are adding noise and the next step is to filter history to high-confidence positives only (long_view=1 AND play_time_ms above the 50th percentile).

mechanism: The Wm matrix (256 params, k=16×16) is initialized to zero, so the model starts identical to the parent. Its per-batch gradient is a rank-1 outer product (target_emb.T @ hist_sum), meaning it learns very slowly and can only capture a single aggregate transformation across all 10 history slots. The symmetric FM term V[target]·V[hist] already encodes the target–history relationship in the shared video_id embedding space; the data does not contain a systematic asymmetric pattern (i.e., a direction in embedding space where "target looking at history" differs from "history looking at target") that Wm can exploit. The slight negative delta (-0.0017, 2.1σ) is consistent with 256 extra parameters introducing marginal overfitting to training noise that does not generalize — but this is at the noise floor, not a confirmed loss. For Wm to have mattered, the target–history interaction would need to be genuinely anisotropic in the embedding space (e.g., "user liked this author's videos" being a different axis than "this video is by that author"), which the shared-embedding FM already captures symmetrically.
transferable_lesson: In this FM with shared video_id embeddings, the symmetric dot product is sufficient for target–history interaction; the binding constraint is the history signal content (how many slots, which source, how recent), not the interaction form — stop trying to make the interaction asymmetric and instead sweep K and history source.
next_experiment: Sweep K ∈ {5, 20, 50} for the long_view history slots (keeping the symmetric FM interaction, no Wm), reporting valid primary for each K. This directly tests whether the history signal is being truncated (K=10 too short) or diluted (K=10 too noisy with stale slots). If K=20 or K=50 beats K=10 by >0.002, the history length was the bottleneck; if all K values cluster within 0.002 of each other, the history content is saturated and the next lever is history source (all impressions vs. positives only) or target-aware retrieval (family b).

mechanism: The delta of -0.0001 (0.1σ) is indistinguishable from seed noise, so no causal mechanism is supported by this data. However, the most plausible explanation for why K=20 fails to beat K=10 is structural to the FM: the second-order interaction term sums ALL pairwise dot products symmetrically with no position weighting. Slots 11–20 are either (a) UNK for the majority of users who lack 11+ long_view positives in train, contributing only V[UNK]·V[target] — a per-video constant already captured by the first-order W vector and thus powerless to change within-user order — or (b) older interactions for power users, whose signal is weaker than the most-recent-10 and is simply added to the symmetric sum, diluting the ratio of strong to weak interaction terms. For K=20 to have mattered, a substantial fraction of users would need 11+ positives AND those older interactions would need to carry ranking signal not already present in the top-10, AND the FM would need a mechanism to weight recency — none of which hold in a standard symmetric FM.
transferable_lesson: In a standard FM the interaction sum is position-symmetric, so adding more history slots cannot concentrate signal on the most relevant ones; to exploit longer history you must either (a) pre-aggregate the history into a smaller number of target-conditioned fields before the FM, or (b) move to a model with explicit position/attention weighting (GRU, DIN) — simply increasing K in the FM is a dilution, not an enrichment.
next_experiment: Test K=5 (fewer, more concentrated long_view history slots) with everything else identical to the parent. If K=5 ≥ K=10, it confirms the dilution mechanism (fewer UNK/old slots → less noise in the symmetric sum) and the right move is to keep K small and add target-awareness via a different architecture. If K=5 < K=10, the extra slots from 5→10 carried real signal and the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g., the shared-embedding-space interaction is too weak to exploit even 10 slots, pointing toward a separate embedding block or attention model).

mechanism: The dilution hypothesis — that K=10 UNK/weak slots in the symmetric FM interaction sum suppress the strongest history×target interactions — is not supported. K=5 and K=10 produce statistically indistinguishable validation primaries (Δ=−0.0007, 0.9σ). For the dilution mechanism to have been the binding constraint, the UNK embedding would have needed to be a large-magnitude, poorly-learned vector whose 5× or 10× accumulation in the sum distorted the interaction term; in practice the shared UNK embedding receives gradient from every UNK occurrence across all users and converges to a small, well-conditioned vector, so removing 5 of the 10 slots neither freed interaction capacity nor lost meaningful signal. Equivalently, the signal in history slots 5–9 (the older long_view positives removed at K=5) was not additive over slots 0–4, consistent with the prior finding that stacking more target-independent recency fields onto this FM does not compound. The number of history slots is not the lever; the symmetric bilinear interaction structure is the ceiling on how much history signal this architecture can extract.
transferable_lesson: In this symmetric-FM setup, sweeping K between 5 and 10 for long_view history is a null experiment; the binding constraint on history signal is the bilinear interaction form itself, not the slot count, so future iterations should change the interaction mechanism (or model family) rather than the number of history items.
next_experiment: Run a K=1 ablation (single most-recent long_view video, everything else identical) to test whether the history interaction term is contributing any differentiating signal at all beyond a per-user constant offset: if K=1 ≈ K=5 ≈ K=10 (all within 0.0016), the history is acting only through the first-order W term and the bilinear interaction is not differentiating items within a user, confirming that the symmetric FM cannot exploit history for within-user ranking and the next step must switch to an asymmetric target-aware scorer (e.g., a 2-layer MLP on [target_emb, mean_hist_emb, target_emb⊙mean_hist_emb] with the same multi-seed ensemble). If K=1 is clearly worse (Δ > 0.002), the interaction term is working and the issue is signal quality, in which case the next step is to switch the history source from long_view to all-impressions (denser sequence, less UNK) at K=10.

mechanism: The deep tower and the FM component share one embedding table but have conflicting optimisation demands. The FM's history signal works through a clean second-order dot-product between the candidate video_id embedding and each history video_id embedding in the shared space — a simple quadratic that converges in ~10 epochs. The deep tower must learn the same candidate×history interaction through a 2-layer MLP, which is a far harder optimisation problem; at 30 epochs it is still improving (no early stop triggered in any seed) and its gradients are still pulling the shared embedding away from the geometry the FM needs. The result is a split: GAUC rises (0.6535 vs the parent's ~0.63) because the undertrained tower adds marginal global discrimination, but nDCG@5 drops sharply (0.5299 vs the parent's ~0.58) because the noisy deep-tower output perturbs the precise top-5 within-user ordering that the well-trained FM was providing. The net primary loss of 0.0131 is dominated by the nDCG damage: the deep tower does not add complementary target-aware signal — it degrades the one mechanism (FM shared-space history interaction) that was actually carrying the history gain, while its own contribution is still in the noise regime.
transferable_lesson: In this task the FM's second-order shared-space interaction with history is the primary signal carrier; any deep component that shares the same embedding table will, unless trained to full convergence or decoupled, pull the embedding geometry away from the FM's needs and destroy the top-5 ordering that drives nDCG@5 — so the deep tower must either be trained to clear convergence (100+ epochs) or be architecturally decoupled (separate embeddings, or FM-frozen fine-tune) before it can add signal rather than subtract it.
next_experiment: Pre-train the parent FM to convergence (as it already does, ~15-20 epochs with early stop), then initialise a DeepFM's embedding table from the converged FM weights and train ONLY the deep tower for 50-100 epochs with the FM component frozen (or the embedding at 10× lower LR). This isolates the question "can a deep tower add target-aware signal on top of a well-trained FM" without the confound of the deep tower's gradients corrupting the FM's embedding geometry during joint training. If primary exceeds 0.6048 by >0.002, the deep tower is adding real signal and the next step is to unfreeze the FM at a small LR for fine-tuning; if it stays at or below 0.6048, the deep tower's capacity is not the bottleneck and the search should pivot to target-aware attention (DIN-style) with a separate embedding for the history, which avoids the shared-table interference entirely.
